Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

prison noun

also jail, gaol, in prison, go to prison, put in prison, lock up, throw into prison, haul off to prison, life imprisonment, house arrest, be held in custody, custody, jailer, take into custody, jailor

classical

Plaut. Amph. 155
Cic. Cat. 2.27
Traupman 174, 191, 195, 196
Traupman 335

carcer, carceris m.

noun, third declension

prison, jail

To throw someone into prison, in carcerem conjicere (Traupman 196) or compingere (Plaut. Amph. 155). In the plural, carcerēs are also the starting gates of a race.

Other words

  • vincula, vinculōrum n. pl. — chains; hence prison

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Caes. BG 4.27: in vincula conjēcerant; Cic. Cat. 4.10 (Lewis & Short)

    in vincula conjicere, to put in irons, to imprison (Caes.; Liv.).

  • custōdia, custōdiae f. — custody; a place of confinement

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.104: in custōdiā necātur (Lewis & Short); Traupman 194

    To take into custody, in custōdiam trādere (Liv. 22.52); to be held in custody, in custōdiā habērī (Traupman 194).

  • custōdiārius, custōdiāriī m. — a jailer

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Inscr. Orell. 1541 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 195; Traupman 335

    Lewis & Short knows it only from an inscription; the classical jailer is the custōs or carcerārius (Plaut.).

Examples

  • quid faciam nunc, sī trēs virī mē in carcerem compēgerint?

    what am I to do now, if the night magistrates lock me up in jail?Plaut. Amph. 155

  • esse carcerem, quem vindicem nefāriōrum ac manifestōrum scelerum majōrēs nostrī esse voluērunt

    that there is a prison, which our ancestors meant to be the avenger of wicked and flagrant crimesCic. Cat. 2.27

  • aliquem in carcerem conjicere

    to throw someone into prisonTraupman 196; cf. Cic. Verr. 2.5.17 (Lewis & Short s.v. conjiciō)

  • aliquem in carcerem compingere

    to lock someone up in prisonTraupman 196; cf. Plaut. Am. 1.1.3 (Lewis & Short s.v. compingō)

  • aliquem in carcerem rapere

    to haul someone off to prisonTraupman 191, 195

  • aliquem damnāre carcerī quoad vīvat

    to sentence someone to life imprisonmentTraupman 196

  • in custōdiā habērī

    to be held in custodyTraupman 194

  • custōdia lībera

    house arrestTraupman 195; cf. Liv. 24.45.8: lībera, private custody (Lewis & Short s.v. custōdia)

  • Mox in carcere sedēbunt.

    They will soon be sitting in jail.Traupman 193

  • in carcerem rapere

    to haul off to prisonTraupman 326

  • lībera custōdia

    house arrestLiv. 24.45.8 (Lewis & Short s.v. custōdia: private custody, confinement in one’s house); Traupman 330

See also prisoner, arrest, punishment, police.
